Two things to know before you start. Writing requires a contributor account, meaning proof that you genuinely contributed to the ecosystem: reading and subscribing require none. And every publication goes through review, without exception: an API token grants the right to submit, never the right to publish.

Il s'utilise en en-tête sur chaque appel: It goes in a header on every call. Start by checking that it answers:
L'inscription est libre et donne un comp: Registration is open and gives you a reader account. A verification email is sent immediately: the link it carries is single-use and activates the account.
L'éditeur est l'organisation ou la perso: The editor is the organisation or person who publishes; your project sheets and announcements belong to it. One never publishes under one's own name: without an editor, nothing can be submitted. The creation form is offered as soon as your contribution proof is accepted, and it stays available at the bottom of your articles page. An integration starting from scratch creates its editor through POST /editors instead. You own the editor you create, and you may attach other contributor accounts to it, who will then publish under the same name.
La compatibilité Dolibarr est une plage: Dolibarr compatibility is a range of major versions, declared either plainly or as genuinely tested. Do not declare as tested what you have not tried: the version filter depends on it.
La fiche décrit le projet de façon perma: The sheet describes the project permanently: name, summary, description, licence, typed links to the repository, the documentation, the shop or support. It carries no Dolibarr compatibility, and that is deliberate: a sheet stays in place for years, so any dated information it held would quietly turn false with nobody to fix it.
La fiche se crée aujourd'hui par l'API u: Today a sheet can only be created through the API. An article can do without one - it is then an editor announcement - but a version release deserves its own.
La maturité va d'alpha à obsolète. Seule: Maturity ranges from alpha to deprecated. Only stable versions show in the feed by default: the reader asks for the rest explicitly.
La qualification est distincte de l'auth: Qualification is distinct from authentication: the account exists first, the proof comes second. The service looks your commit author address up in an index harvested from git clones of the reference repositories - never through a forge API, so that verification survives the disappearance of any host.
La réponse porte les deux valeurs dont d: The answer carries the two values every write depends on: is_contributor, and the list of your editors with their identifier. Note that identifier down, the following calls ask for it.
La soumission réserve un jeton de public: Submission reserves a publication token. Three moderator approvals publish automatically; any edit resets the approvals.
Le code du service est publié sous licen: The service code is published under the GNU AGPL v3 licence.
Le corps est en Markdown. Les liens sort: The body is Markdown. Outgoing links are all marked nofollow, and only images deposited on the service may illustrate an article.
Le jeton sert à publier depuis votre cha: The token lets you publish from your integration chain, and the next step needs one. Name it after its use: the secret is shown once, at creation, and can be revoked at any time.
Le parcours complet, étape par étape: The complete path, step by step
Ici, l'information est toujours datée :: Here, information is always dated: your announcement states the module's compatibility and maturity on the day you publish it. DoliNews does not claim to describe a module's current state, only what you have announced about it, and when. Your project sheet, by contrast, is permanent: it carries neither compatibility nor maturity.
Le type distingue la sortie de version d: The type separates a version release from an editor announcement; the nature of the publication - security, bugfix, feature, compatibility, end of life - only applies to a version.
Les contenus publiés - articles, fiches: Published contents - articles, project sheets, translations - are distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 licence (CC BY-SA 4.0). The author keeps their copyright and authorship; by submitting, they place their content under that licence, which allows the service and third parties to reproduce, distribute and adapt it, provided the author is credited and the same licence is kept.
Les maturités non stables sont exclues d: Non-stable maturities are excluded from the feed by default.
Les raccourcisseurs d'URL sont refusés,: URL shorteners are refused, and a Dolistore listing already claimed by another editor raises a conflict for moderation to settle.
On publie au nom d'un éditeur. Créez le: One publishes under an editor. Create yours to begin: you will own it.

Par le site depuis la page de vos articl: From the site, on your articles page, or through the API. The content is the same either way, and the summary is mandatory: it is what the reader skims in the feed, and its absence is what makes most release logs unreadable.
Quatre étapes. Un jeton donne le droit d: Four steps. A token grants the right to submit: publication comes from the review, never from the call.

Un compte lecteur sert aux abonnements :: A reader account is for subscriptions: following projects and editors, with a personal feed. Publishing requires a contribution verification, separate and later.
Un éditeur possédé par compte : le crédi: One owned editor per account: the publication credit and the queue ceiling are counted per editor. You join the others on their owner's invitation.
Une annonce illustrée se publie en deux: An illustrated announcement is published in two steps: deposit the images, then create the article citing their addresses in the body and their identifiers in media_ids. Without those identifiers the images stay orphaned and are erased after twenty-four hours.
Une capture d'un Dolibarr en service con: A screenshot of a Dolibarr in service almost always contains real data - thirdparties, amounts, addresses. Clean it up before sending it.

Une fois l'adresse reconnue, il reste à: Once the address is recognised, you still have to prove it is yours. Two levels:
Une fois publié, un article ne se modifi: Once published, an article is never edited in place: you propose a revision, which goes back through review, the article carries the mention of its correction and the original version stays readable. A translation is an article in its own right, tied to its original, and it goes through review too; an untranslated announcement is never penalised in distribution.
Utilisez de préférence l'adresse avec la: Prefer the address you sign your commits with. If that address is already known to the author index, your account becomes a contributor account the moment you verify the email, and the next step does not concern you.
Vos annonces partent de l'espace article: Your announcements start from the article space.
Votre adresse de commit est une redirect: Your commit address is an anonymised redirect, of the kind forges hand out: it receives no mail, so only the GPG signature or manual validation remain.
Votre adresse n'apparaît dans aucun dépô: Your address appears in no reference repository: ask the team for manual validation from that same page, explaining your situation. This is the route meant for editors without a public repository.
Votre adresse n'est jamais conservée en: Your address is never kept in clear text, neither in the index nor on the proof: only its peppered hash is stored.
Votre article entre dans la file et troi: Your article enters the queue and three moderators must accept it for it to appear. Exchanges happen in a private thread between you and the team: you answer there, you fix, you resubmit. Editing a pending article opens a new review round, because an accord bears on a precise text.
Votre compte peut publier : il porte une: Your account can publish: it holds an active contribution proof.

Toute publication passe par une revue a: Every publication goes through a prior review, on the pull request model: submission, team review, acceptance by three moderators, automatic publication.
